subject: fluid_mechanics
title: Minor Losses in Fluid Flow in Pipes
aim: To determine the Loss Coefficient (K) of a fluid flowing through pipe fittings (sudden contraction / enlargement).
apparatus: Pipe test section with sudden contraction/enlargement (Larger D = 0.04 m, Smaller d = 0.02 m)
Measuring tank (0.4 m × 0.4 m) with piezometer and stopwatch
Flow control valves and pressure tappings
theory:
When a fluid flows through pipe fittings, bends, valves, or sudden changes in section (enlargements and contractions), it experiences local disturbances, flow separation, and eddy formation that cause additional head losses. These are termed 'minor losses'.

Differential Manometer Reading:
\Delta h = |h_2 - h_1| \quad (\text{cm})

Equivalent Head Loss in meters of water:
h_f = \frac{\Delta h}{100} \times 12.6 \quad (\text{m})

Actual Volumetric Flow Rate:
Q = \frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{A_{tank} \times rise}{t} = \frac{0.4 \times 0.4 \times 0.1}{t} = \frac{0.016}{t} \quad (\text{m}^3/\text{s})

Velocities in Larger and Smaller Pipes:
V_1 = \frac{Q}{A_1} = \frac{Q}{\frac{\pi D^2}{4}} = \frac{Q}{1.256 \times 10^{-3}} \quad (\text{m/s})
V_2 = \frac{Q}{A_2} = \frac{Q}{\frac{\pi d^2}{4}} = \frac{Q}{3.14 \times 10^{-4}} \quad (\text{m/s})

Loss Coefficient (K):
h_f = K \frac{V_2^2 - V_1^2}{2g} \implies K = \frac{h_f}{\frac{V_2^2 - V_1^2}{2g}}
procedure: Switch on the power supply and start the centrifugal pump.
Adjust the delivery flow control valve and purge all air bubbles from the manometer lines.
Record the manometer limb readings h1 and h2 in cm.
Close the drain valve of the measuring tank and note down the time taken for 10 cm (0.1 m) water level rise.
Repeat the procedure for 5 different flow rates.
Calculate Δh, hf, Q, V1, V2, and the Loss Coefficient K for each trial.

formulas.label: Differential Manometer Level (Δh)
formulas.derivation:
Direct differential height reading between two manometer limbs:

\Delta h = |h_2 - h_1| \text{ (cm)}

formulas.label: Manometer Head Loss (hf)
formulas.derivation:
Equivalent water head loss across the pipe fitting:

h_f = \frac{\Delta h}{100} \times (S_{Hg} - S_w) = \frac{\Delta h}{100} \times 12.6 \text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates head loss across pipe fitting.
assumptions: Mercury specific gravity = 13.6, water specific gravity = 1.0
formulas.practical_application: Quantifies energy head loss caused by pipe fitting.

formulas.label: Actual Volumetric Discharge (Q)
formulas.derivation:
Discharge measured by time t for 10 cm water level rise in 0.4 m × 0.4 m tank:

Q = \frac{0.4 \times 0.4 \times 0.1}{t} = \frac{0.016}{t} \text{ (m³/s)}

formulas.label: Velocity in Larger Pipe (V1)
formulas.purpose: Determines flow velocity in upstream larger pipe.

formulas.label: Velocity in Smaller Pipe (V2)
formulas.purpose: Determines flow velocity in downstream smaller pipe.

formulas.label: Loss Coefficient (K)
formulas.derivation:
Loss coefficient relating minor head loss to difference in velocity heads:

h_f = K \frac{V_2^2 - V_1^2}{2g} \implies K = \frac{h_f \times 2g}{V_2^2 - V_1^2}
formulas.practical_application: Crucial for sizing piping fittings and calculating pressure drop in industrial piping systems.

precautions: Operate the control valves gradually to prevent air locking in the manometer tubes.
Ensure complete removal of air bubbles from the pressure tap tubing before recording limb readings.
Maintain steady water flow while timing the water rise in the measuring tank.
